Create an automation rule.

Set exactly one of `session_id` (a tracing project) or `dataset_id`.
`sampling_rate` (0-1) and `filter` choose which runs it acts on; for
example `filter` eq(status, "error") matches runs that errored. The rule
applies to new runs while `is_enabled` is true, which is the default, so
set it to false to create a paused rule. Set `backfill_from` to also apply
it to runs since that time.

Delete an automation rule.

The rule stops applying immediately. Actions it already took (feedback,
dataset examples, queue items) are kept. Evaluators created for the rule
are deleted; a shared evaluator is kept. To stop a rule reversibly, set
`is_enabled` to false instead.

List the automation rules in the workspace.

An automation rule samples runs from a tracing project (or a dataset's
experiments), filters them, and applies actions: evaluators, adding to a
dataset or annotation queue, webhooks, and alerts. Returns every matching
rule in one response (not paginated); narrow it with the filters.

operations.summary: Get an automation rule's last application
operations.description:
Get the most recent application of an automation rule.

Use it to check whether a rule is running and which runs it last acted on.
`backfill` returns the last backfill application instead of the live one.

Apply an automation rule now instead of waiting for its schedule.

Queues one application over runs since the rule last ran and returns
before it finishes. Check progress with the last-applied endpoint.

Apply several automation rules now.

Pass either `rule_ids`, or `dataset_id` to trigger every rule on that
dataset. Each application is queued and the call returns before they
finish.

Update an automation rule.

Replaces the rule's whole configuration: every field you omit is reset
to its default. An omitted `is_enabled` turns the rule back on and an
omitted `filter` clears it, so send every field you want to keep,
including `session_id` or `dataset_id`. Changes apply to runs processed
after the update. Set `is_enabled` to false to pause a rule without
deleting it.
